text:
- chief complaint: pain at the end of the patient's right middle finger after a motor vehicle accident four to five days ago.
- history of present illness: the patient was stopped at a four-way stop when rear-ended, and the impact caused the patient's right middle finger to strike the car ceiling. There were no other injuries, and the patient's car sustained minor trunk damage. An x-ray showed a distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger.
- physical examination: tenderness over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger; the rest of the exam was normal.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: pain in the right middle finger, most pronounced at the fingertip.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: tramadol 50 mg every six hours as needed for pain, eight tablets dispensed (about two days' supply).
- follow-up instructions: finger splint applied; return in two weeks for a follow-up x-ray.
